text:
Low carbohydrate intake shifts muscles toward fat and away from glycogen during exercise, so the first listed option (greater reliance on muscle glycogen) is backwards. The second option gets the fat-oxidation direction right, but its claimed benefit for high-intensity performance isn't well supported, and its mechanism is wrong because low dietary carbohydrate lowers glycogen stores rather than speeding up glycogen breakdown. Neither option is correct as written, so the team note likely contains an error.

CONFIDENCE: 60
